basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Records where an enterprise assertion came from and on what evidence, without deciding whether it is true.
Gives every change of source, acquisition, version or content digest a new capture ID instead of overwriting.
Keeps confidence qualified by the method that produced it, so numbers from different schemes are never added up.

may: Show the acquisition account and evidence behind an assertion.
Append an authorized correction or withdrawal and propose re-review.
Return insufficient-context with the known gaps when evidence is missing.
mustNot: Infer that a source is true because it is recorded here.
Count assertions with shared inputs as independent confirmation.
Rewrite a historical account when reading it.
requiresHuman: Withdrawing an assertion that others rely on.
Adopting an assertion as authoritative for a business decision.

considerations: Provenance records can expose who said what about whom; access must follow the rules of the underlying data.
A confident-looking assertion without visible evidence can mislead decisions about people.
Withdrawn assertions stay visible as history so that blame and correction remain traceable.
affectedParties: Employees and contractors whose actions or data appear in company records
Customers, suppliers and partners named in company records
Auditors, regulators and courts that rely on the record later

owners.steward: The data governance function of the company stewards provenance records; each assertion stays owned by its source system.
masterSystems: Source systems that issue the assertions

items: Capture ID per acquisition, changed whenever source identity, version or content digest changes.
External source identity kept separately from the capture.

properties.reason: Institutional or informational subject: it has no physical body to measure.

items: A provenance record points to one assertion and lists its source, acquisition time, method and evidence.
It is confused with the assertion itself and with an audit log of system access.
Circular confirmation when two records share one upstream source.
False authority when provenance is displayed as proof.
Applies to facts held in a Company Dimension that come from internal or external sources.

sections.whatItIs: A companion contract for a Company Dimension that records where each enterprise assertion came from: the source, how and when it was acquired, the evidence kept and the method-qualified confidence, without judging whether the assertion is true.

sources.title: Research record EM-XCT-03: independent provider studies, audits and reconciled findings
sources.note: Evidence behind the release; claims in the card trace to it.
